video_title: Investigating Magic Johnson, the Dodgers Owner... and Your Nest Egg | PTFO

quotes.speaker: Sam Koppelman
quotes.summary_phrase: Mark Walter's Lakers purchase and subsequent sale raised red flags
quotes.excerpt: It's not every summer vacation when a multi-billionaire has their phone and laptop seized on their private jet.
quotes.quote: It's not every summer vacation when a multi-billionaire has their phone and laptop seized on their private jet. And then it comes out that that same billionaire is selling the Lakers a year after buying the team. That felt like break glass in case of emergency.

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers sold to Josh Kushner and Bob Iger for $12.5 billion
quotes.excerpt: The Lakers got sold for a record $12.5 billion to Josh Kushner and Bob Iger.
quotes.quote: The Lakers got sold for a record $12.5 billion to Josh Kushner and Bob Iger.

quotes.speaker: Sam Koppelman
quotes.summary_phrase: Sports teams have become incredibly expensive assets for owners
quotes.excerpt: Sports teams used to be owned by the richest guy in a town. They've become this incredibly expensive asset.
quotes.quote: Sports teams used to be owned by the richest guy in a town. They loved their team so much and they became successful or their parents were successful and then they used that money to buy the team. But the thing is that sports teams have become this incredibly expensive asset. And so these owners have to go to incredible extremes to raise money to buy these teams.

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: Billionaire owners use leverage to fund sports team purchases
quotes.excerpt: They are leveraging other assets to pay these unprecedented prices.
quotes.quote: The term people just need to understand here briefly is leverage. They are leveraging other assets to pay these unprecedented prices. And leveraging, Sam, just means they're using the money that they have to borrow more of it.

quotes.speaker: Sam Koppelman
quotes.summary_phrase: Mark Walter uses insurance money to fund sports investments
quotes.excerpt: With Mark Walter, the big pool of money that he has access to is insurance money.
quotes.quote: With Mark Walter, the big pool of money that he has access to is insurance money. The way this works is basically Americans buy life insurance policies. They come in two forms. One is if something tragic happens to you, you've paid into these insurance plans and money will be paid out to your family members who are left behind. The other way is while you're working, you can pay money into a life insurer, something called annuities, and you end up getting paid out annuities later in your life. So you're investing today for some kind of payout tomorrow.

quotes.speaker: Sam Koppelman
quotes.summary_phrase: Using insurance money for affiliated business investments requires disclosure
quotes.excerpt: There's one category of investment you're not allowed to make without proper disclosure.
quotes.quote: There's one category of investment you're not allowed to make without proper disclosure. And that's if you're using insurance money to invest in another one of your own businesses. If I owned an insurance company and also a Szechuan fish stew soup dumpling restaurant, I couldn't use your parents and grandparents' insurance payments to invest in my dream of succulent soup dumplings filled with Szechuan fish stew unless I disclosed that very clearly.

quotes.speaker: Sam Koppelman
quotes.summary_phrase: Mark Walter and Guggenheim Partners underreported affiliated transactions
quotes.excerpt: Mark Walter and Guggenheim Partners severely underreported just how much money was mislabeled and never disclosed.
quotes.quote: It seems like happened is that Mark Walter and Guggenheim Partners severely underreported just how much money was mislabeled and never disclosed as an affiliated transaction. And that total, the total of affiliated transactions has gone from what his insurers had estimated to be around $3 billion to now tens of billions of dollars.

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: Mark Walter's sports team purchases have been a catalyst for valuation growth
quotes.excerpt: The biggest catalyst behind this century's boom in sports team valuations is arguably Mark Walter himself.
quotes.quote: The biggest catalyst behind this century's boom in sports team valuations is arguably Mark Walter himself. He bought the Lakers at a then-record $10 billion valuation last fall. Before that, 2022, he bought a chunk of Chelsea in Premier League football at a then-record valuation of well over $3 billion.

quotes.speaker: David Samson
quotes.summary_phrase: Dodgers were in bankruptcy in 2012 due to Frank McCourt's divorce
quotes.excerpt: The Dodgers were in Chapter 11 bankruptcy back in 2012 because the owner was Frank McCourt.
quotes.quote: The Dodgers were in Chapter 11 bankruptcy back in 2012 because the owner was Frank McCourt, who was involved in a divorce from his wife Jamie McCourt. They're arguing, figuring out how to split up assets, and baseball wanted to get out from under the McCourts.

quotes.speaker: David Samson
quotes.summary_phrase: Mark Walter, Stephen Cohen, and Stan Kroenke bid for the Dodgers
quotes.excerpt: Mark Walter and Guggenheim were a bidder. The now owner of the Mets, Stephen Cohen, Stan Kroenke was a bidder.
quotes.quote: Mark Walter and Guggenheim were a bidder. The now owner of the Mets, Stephen Cohen, Stan Kroenke was a bidder for the Dodgers. The result was that all three parties were right around the same number. Let's call it $1.5 billion.

quotes.speaker: David Samson
quotes.summary_phrase: Mark Walter and Guggenheim secured a deal with MLB for revenue sharing
quotes.excerpt: Mark Walter and Guggenheim got a deal themselves from Major League Baseball where they had a cap.
quotes.quote: Mark Walter and Guggenheim got a deal themselves from Major League Baseball where they had a cap given to them of how much broadcast revenue would be subject to revenue sharing.

quotes.speaker: Sam Koppelman
quotes.summary_phrase: MLB allowed the Dodgers to keep more TV revenue in exchange for a higher purchase price
quotes.excerpt: The MLB allowed the Dodgers to keep more of the money it was making from its TV rights deal.
quotes.quote: The MLB allowed the Dodgers to keep more of the money it was making from its TV rights deal in exchange for Mark Walter buying the team at a higher price.

quotes.speaker: David Samson
quotes.summary_phrase: David Samson negotiated a TV deal with Fox for the Marlins
quotes.excerpt: I negotiated my tushy off with Fox to get 80.
quotes.quote: I negotiated my tushy off with Fox to get 80.

quotes.speaker: David Samson
quotes.summary_phrase: Fox executives were furious about the Dodgers' TV deal
quotes.excerpt: Don't bring up the Time Warner deal. We're not using that as anything.
quotes.quote: You're asking whether it makes sense what Time Warner did and you're talking to someone who was in the room with Fox executives when news of this had come out like the day before. And the guy who was negotiating with looked at me and said, 'Don't, don't, don't, David. Do not bring up the Time Warner deal. We're not using that as anything. That is an overpay that they're going to live to regret from the day they sign it. We're pissed that we lost the Dodgers, but we wouldn't have paid that, no chance.'

quotes.speaker: Sam Koppelman
quotes.summary_phrase: Time Warner's high distribution fees led to a blackout for Dodgers fans
quotes.excerpt: Time Warner paid a certain amount of money for the Dodgers' rights and then they were going to try.
quotes.quote: Time Warner paid a certain amount of money for the Dodgers' rights and then they were going to try to charge the other channels some kind of profit and those other channels were like absolutely not.

quotes.speaker: Sam Koppelman
quotes.summary_phrase: EquiTrust loaned $350 million to American Media Productions
quotes.excerpt: A combined total of $350 million.
quotes.quote: A combined total of $350 million.

quotes.speaker: Sam Koppelman
quotes.summary_phrase: Mark Walter tried to terminate the Dodgers' TV deal early
quotes.excerpt: Mark Walter engaged Charter Communications in talks to 'let the cable company out of the Lakers and Dodgers'.
quotes.quote: Mark Walter engaged Charter Communications in talks to 'let the cable company out of the Lakers and Dodgers' local TV deals early for a lump sum payout, but those talks 'went nowhere,' according to John Ourand of PUCK.

quotes.speaker: Sam Koppelman
quotes.summary_phrase: Magic Johnson became a controlling shareholder of EquiTrust
quotes.excerpt: EquiTrust also announced that Earvin Johnson is becoming a controlling shareholder of the company.
quotes.quote: EquiTrust also announced that Earvin Johnson is becoming a controlling shareholder of the company.

quotes.speaker: Sam Koppelman
quotes.summary_phrase: EquiTrust became the biggest asset in Magic Johnson Enterprises
quotes.excerpt: EquiTrust is now the biggest asset in the Magic Johnson Enterprises portfolio.
quotes.quote: EquiTrust is now the biggest asset in the Magic Johnson Enterprises portfolio, and with Johnson as its majority owner, it represents just how far he has come as a businessman.

quotes.speaker: Sam Koppelman
quotes.summary_phrase: Billionaires use complex corporate structures to obscure money flow
quotes.excerpt: Billionaires are very good at making LLCs and entities and making money flow in a way that's much less.
quotes.quote: Billionaires are very good at making LLCs and entities and making money flow in a way that's much less direct than you sending money to your friend on Venmo. But it's not actually that different. It's actually people paying money to other people to get something in return.

quotes.speaker: Pablo Torre
quotes.summary_phrase: White House championship ring ceremonies as political invitations
quotes.excerpt: seems something like an invitation for Trump to do something that Magic Johnson and Eric Holland
quotes.quote: Which, in retrospect, at least to me, seems something like an invitation for Trump to do something that Magic Johnson and Eric Holland and David Rone and even our voice-modulated compliant attorney source at Guggenheim had all done before to varying degrees of regret.
